numbers.converterHint: Type any number to see and hear it in German.
numbers.r1text: These numbers are words of their own.
numbers.r2text: drei + zehn = dreizehn. Careful: sechzehn (not sechs-), siebzehn (not sieben-).
numbers.r3text: zwanzig, vierzig, fünfzig … Careful: dreißig (-ßig), sechzig, siebzig.
numbers.r4text: Backwards! 47 = sieben-und-vierzig (“seven and forty”). 1 → ein: einundzwanzig.
numbers.r5text: 347 = dreihundert + siebenundvierzig. 100 = (ein)hundert. Always written as one word.
numbers.r7text: 1100–1999: neunzehnhundert… (“nineteen hundred…”). From 2000: zweitausend… “Ich bin 1998 geboren.” – no “in”.
numbers.r8text: The cents are said without “Cent”: drei Euro fünfzig.
numbers.r9text: Usually digit by digit, sometimes in pairs. On the phone people often say “zwo” for “zwei”.

q.numberPieces: Order the pieces: hundreds, then ones + und + tens
q.numberPiecesWhy: In German the ones come before the tens: 47 = sieben-und-vierzig (“seven and forty”).
q.orderFromText: Build a sentence from the text
q.orderWords: Put the words in the right order

q.pluralWhy: In the plural the article is always “die”.

q.yearWhy: Years 1100–1999 are said in hundreds (neunzehnhundert…), from 2000 like normal numbers.
